# 0.15.151

**A forwarded message is judged honestly again.**

A forward carries the author's own envelope and their signature over it, and
the device that receives it checks that signature itself rather than taking
anyone's word. It was checking against the author's *account* key — but every
message this application sends is signed by the *device* that made it. So the
check failed on every genuine message, and the copy was drawn with the one
verdict a certificate must never give wrongly: "Signature does not match".

A reader who has never met the author cannot know that a device is really
theirs, so the author's own signed device list now travels with the
certificate. It cannot be forged: it names the account it belongs to, that
account signed it, every certificate inside it is checked, and the key it has
to match is already in the same certificate and already checked to belong to
the author.

Separately, and just as important: when no list is held, or it does not name
the device, the copy is now left **unjudged** rather than called false. Not
knowing and knowing it is wrong are different things, and only one of them was
being said.

Forwarding a message with a link card on it also works again (0.15.149): the
card was being stripped out of the signed envelope, and the card is inside the
signature.
